Among these are: a) acceleration changes at segmentation points due to the effects of force pick-up, opening switch risetime and current feed geometry, b) opening switches with pulse compressions of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and c) relations which determine sizing of segements and magnetic energy stores. In addition, we will discuss the relative merits of inverse railgun pulse generators (flux compressors) and HPG's for charging magnetic stores.

articleTitle: Measurement of the temperature distribution of a sintering process by magnetometer
abstract: We present in this paper a new method to detect the temperature distribution of a sintering bed by measuring the thickness of the sintered bed. This method is based on the fact that the sintered ore contains magnetite with its magnetic property and that the heat pattern depends on the thickness of the sintered bed. By getting a fluxgate magnetometer installed over the sintering bed and measuring the magnetic field deviation produced by the sintering bed, we can detect the thickness of the sintered bed and hence its temperature distribution directly and continuously, and improve the productivity and quality of the sintering process. For this application we have developed a new magnetometer, which has two cores wire-wound differentially to cancel the background magnetic field and made of Mo-Permalloy sheet.

articleTitle: Susceptibility of amorphous magnetic materials over a wide frequency range
abstract: Initial susceptibilities of rapidly quenched amorphous magnetic materials have been measured over the frequency range from 1 kHz to 1 GHz at room temperature. Materials were amorphous magnetic ribbons of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">66</inf>Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf>, and Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">38</inf>Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</inf>. At frequencies above 300 MHz, resonance phenomena (sharp drop of the susceptibility to zero) have been observed for all materials examined. The resonance frequencies agree well with calculated values for ferromagnetic resonance.

articleTitle: Spontaneous hall effect of non-S-state rare earths in amorphous GdAu
abstract: The spontaneous Hall effect has been studied in ferromagnetic Gd-An amorphous films containing up to 20 atomic % of Tb, Ho, Er, Tm or Nd replacing Gd. It has been found that the non-S-state rare earths have the same effectiveness as a Hall scatter as the replaced Gd. Decreases in the spontaneous Hall conductivity (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{s}/\rho^{2}</tex>) in the ternary alloys are associated with decreases in Curie temperature as found earlier for the original Gd-Au binary system. The Curie temperature is used as a measure of the conduction electron polarization. It is these spin polarized electrons of the ferromagnetic Gd-Au host which is one of the important Hall parameters in its interaction with the non-S-state rare earths. The light rare earth Nd has an exceptionally high value of Hall conductivity.

articleTitle: A small size 7 Tesla flux-concentrator of modular construction fed by a small thyristor pulse generator
abstract: The generation of high magnetic pulsed fields in circularly cylindrical volumes of short length with a conventional Bitter coil design leads to difficult technical problems. We will show that in these cases a special design of a flux concentrator may be an alternative solution. The existing flux concentrator systems are composed of a cylindrical conducting core (with inner bore and radial slot) as single turn secondary coil, surrounded by an exciting multi-turn primary coil. Applying a pulsed voltage to the primary the induced current - due to the slot - will be urged to flow around the inner bore in a thin layer (skin-effect). Since on the outer periphery exciting and induced current have opposite directions nearly the total flux will be concentrated in the inner bore. Obviously the efficiency of current transfer from primary to core depends on coupling. Therefore a multilayer primary coil is an improper means of raising the total excitation. However the modular construction proposed here allows the total excitation to be increased with maintaining the efficiency by interlacing further secondary and primary coils. Together with a small thyristor pulse generator we thus arrive at a small size simple and inexpensive high field system which may easily be adapted to various needs in laboratory and instrumentation applications.

articleTitle: Calculation of the forces and the field in a cylindrical shell with a general excitation by using an integral formulation
abstract: In this work an attempt is made for the Calculation of the forces and the current density in a cylindrical shell, when the excitation is a circular cylinder which is placed inside the shell at an arbitrary position. The distribution of the current density is calculated either inside the shell or inside the conductor of the excitation. For this purpose an integral formulation is used. For the numerical treatment of the problem the method of moments is applied.

articleTitle: Superconductive helical flow magnetic ore separator
abstract: A high field helical flow-through separator to concentrate weakly magnetic ores is described. The process is to flow slurry helically around a current carrying conductor in a cylindrical annulus. The magnetic field gradient forces magnetic particles inwards towards the conductor. Nonmagnetic particles (gangue, sands, etc.) are deflected outwards by centrifugal force. Separation occurs at the exit end of the channel where a divider separates inboard from outboard slurry. The experimental part of this experimental and theoretical study is reported here. Carefully sized synthetic ore particles with and without sand in a slurry are used. Experiments cover a wide range of particle sizes (100 - 800 microns), magnetic moments (1.4 - 4.8 Am<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/kg), velocities (1.5 - 4 m/sec), magnetic flux densities (0 - 1.6 T), input solid concentrations (2.6 - 15% by weight), and input grades (16.5 - 100%). Satisfactory separation is found within the above parameter regions.

articleTitle: Switching overview - Fundamental issues
The influence of the skin effect on eddy current losses in the plane for single and multidomain wall models
abstract: Eddy current losses have been determined with the phenomenon of the skin effect for single and multidomain wall models taken into account. The domains were assumed to be separated by 180° Bloch walls. The calculations made possible plotting the dependence of eddy current losses on the domain width/sheet thickness ratio for different values of the skin effect coefficient. The results obtained are consistent with those provided by Agarwal and Rabins [3] for the single-domain wall model and with those presented by Pry and Bean [2] for the multidomain wall model. A value of the skin effect coefficient was found for which the skin effect considerably affects eddy current losses.

articleTitle: Support-electrode torque on a spherical superconducting gyroscope
abstract: In a proposed satellite experiment, a spherical superconducting gyroscope is to be levitated by servo-controlled voltages applied to superconducting electrodes. Gyroscope readout will utilize the magnetic field that is generated by a rotating superconductor. However exclusion of this field from the electrodes via the Meissner effect will produce a torque on the gyroscope. That torque is calculated in this paper.

articleTitle: Some considerations on crosstalk in multihead magnetic digital recording
abstract: Crosstalk in the recording process and the playback process was studied in multihead digital tape recorder applications. The limitation of track density in multitrack digital recording is determined by intertrack crosstalk. Improvement of crosstalk through the head and the electronic circuit designs is described.

articleTitle: Measurement of perpendicularity of magnetic field in polar Kerr magnetooptical loop tracer using nickel film with oblique magnetic anisotropy
abstract: This paper introduces an original method to measure the degree of perpendicularity of magnetic field in the polar Kerr magnetooptical hysteresis loop tracer using an evaporated nickel thin film with oblique uniaxial magnetic anisotropy. In this method, the inclination angle of the magnetic field from the film normal of the sample can be obtained from the ratio of the maximum coercivity to the minimum one of the Hall or polar Kerr loop when the Ni film is rotated on the sample stage.

articleTitle: Scaling of permalloy propagators for bubble devices
abstract: The extent to which field access permalloy bubble devices can be scaled in density depends fundamentally on the scaling characteristics of the basic propagator. The effects of bubble film parameters and thin film thicknesses when the minor loop propagator period is varied are measured for bit loading and minimum drive. Various asymmetric chevrons propagators with period sizes ranging from 5.5 to 7.5 μm, with stripe widths varying between 1.2 and 2.8 μm, and with spacer thicknesses covering 1500 to 5000 Å are compared. An accurate comparison was obtained by placing different period sizes and propagator designs on the same wafer. Propagation bias field and drive field margins are reported with start/stop operation and data patterns of increasing complexity. Data shows that material and fabrication requirements should be based on margins characteristic of fully loaded bubble patterns rather than on performance corresponding to lightly loaded patterns.

articleTitle: Importance of the crystalline anisotropy in commercial Ni Fe alloys
abstract: Ni-Fe alloys from 45 % to 80 % Nickel exhibit some of the most versatile magnetic properties. It is shown that the general trends of their magnetic properties can be largely interpreted in terms of the balance between the magnetocrystalline K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>and the induced Ku anisotropies. Using the 55-45 Ni-Fe alloy as an example, a simple model is developed which derives the Ku and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>variations for different annealing treatments. Taking into consideration the recrystallization textures of the industrial material, an estimation of the d.c. and a.c. permeability variations with the magnetic annealing parameters is given and a good agreement with experimental results is observed.

articleTitle: Device for the automatic determination of the magnetic properties of electrical steel sheet
abstract: In order to investigate the magnetic properties of soft magnetic materials, especially of electrical steel sheet, with high accuracy and minimal manual operation, we have developed a computerized control and measuring device which cooperates with all commonly used magnetization equipment such as an Epstein frame, single sheet yoke etc. The device delivers a sinusoidal voltage with programmable frequency and amplitude which is used to control a power amplifier supplying the magnetizing current. The following magnetic quantities are derived from the induced voltage in a secondary winding and from the voltage drop at a series shunt in the primary circuit or, alternatively, from a tangential field sensing coil: peak value of magnetic flux density, rms value of induced voltage, remanent induction, peak value of magnetic field strength, rms value of magnetic field strength, coercive field strength, and total maqnetic loss. All quantities are converted to dc voltages for analog readout and, after digitization, for computer storage. The time dependence of H(t) or dH(t)/dt and B(t) or dB(t)/dt can be sampled at up to 256 points per period, allowing the reconstruction of the hysteresis loop; thus all quantities can be obtained by analog and digital signal processing as well. The frequency range of the apparatus is 8 Hz to 1023 Hz.

articleTitle: Extended temperature operation of one megabit bubble memory devices
abstract: We have demonstrated that the operating temperature range of MBM2011A commercial (0-70°C) one megabit bubble memory devices may be significantly extended by application of temperature compensation to the chip biasing field and function currents. Compensation of biasing field is achieved using the internal z-bias coil of the device. Full functionality and non-volatility of devices over a -55°C to +85°C case temperature range have been achieved using predominantly linear tracking rules. This greatly increased operating temperature range significantly extends the application range of bubble technology.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Co-P plated floppy disks
abstract: A Co-P plated floppy disk has been manufactured. The design concept of the disk is described. Metallic recording medium enables one to achieve higher recording density as compared with conventional floppy disk media. The performances of the metallic floppy and γ-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>covered disks are compared. Above 450 BPM linear recording density can be obtained at D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>using Co-P film floppy disk.

articleTitle: The effects of substructure on the high density core loss properties of commercial grain-oriented 3% SiFe
abstract: Commercially-produced grain-oriented 3% SiFe is batch annealed in coil form thereby generating single crystal grains with slight amounts of misorientation as measured from grain edge to grain interior. When heat flattened, lattice bending occurs along with the generation of a dislocation substructure, the quantity and arrangement of which depend on deformation rate, amount of deformation and stress relief annealing temperature. The 60 Hz core losses at 1.5 and 1.7T were found to be very sensitive to the latter two parameters. Core losses were modeled as a function of dislocation substructure. A strong linear correlation between supplemental losses, which are associated with 90° domain wall motion, and dislocation density was found without regard to dislocation arrangement. A weaker correlation was found between the interaction of 180° domain walls and dislocation density, perhaps indicating that dislocation arrangement is important here.

articleTitle: Sendust sputtered ferrite flying erase head
abstract: A flying erase head (F.E.H.) for the high Hc metal powder tape of 8mm Video was developed by sputtering sendust on the leading side of the ferrite head gap. The F.E.H. is suited to the portable and camera combined VTRs because it makes possible to consume less power, insert a video signal in a recorded tape and simplify a tape transport system.

articleTitle: Determination of defect length in disk coatings by autocorrelation
abstract: A technique is described for measuring the weighted defect length in particulate disk coatings by calculating the autocorrelation of the noise spectra. Data from several disks are presented. The noise-derived defect length assists the identification of the dominant noise generators in the disk coating. Examples are given where the noise is dominated by the alumina particles, pinholes (and similar voids), and buffing damage. Noise management is facilitated with this information.

articleTitle: Magnetic and mechanical properties in crystallized amorphous Fe-Co-Ni-Al based ribbons
abstract: The technique of crystallization of amorphous alloys has been applied to (Fe,Co,Ni,Cu)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x-y</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Me<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>alloys (Me=B, C, Si, P) in order to develop mechanically workable hard magnetic materials. The alloys with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x\leq7</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y\approx20</tex>can be quenched into ductile amorphous or semi-amorphous ribbons using a single roller method. As-prepared ribbons have no hard magnetic properties before annealing. Controlled crystallization of the ribbons results in metastable multiphase microstructure and develops hard magnetic properties. The coercive forces obtained depend strongly on glass forming elements. Of the elements investigated, boron is the most effective for magnetic hardening. (Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">59</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">26</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">73</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>ribbon, which is initially semi-amorphous, has the minimum bending diameter of 1 mm and the tensile strength of 100 kg/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>before crystallization annealing, and shows<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>of 450 Oe, Br of 7 kG, and (BH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>of 1.2 MGOe after crystallization.

articleTitle: Analysis of readback from duplex vertical recording films
abstract: Readback from vertical recording films with a permeable sublayer is analyzed using boundary integral methods. Experimental data are in good agreement and show that spacing losses may be either more or less than the Wallace loss, depending upon the geometry.

articleTitle: On a DC free block modulation code
abstract: A rate 8/10 modulation code, which is suitable for a recording channel with a transformer-coupled rotary head, is developed. The code has the following advantages. Because<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T_{\max}</tex>is short, overwrite noise, when it is overwritten, is small and the peak shift of the playback signal is also small. Disturbance of recording current caused by low frequency cut-off characteristics of recording circuit is small since the power spectrum in the low frequency region is low. Because there is a particular code pattern, which appears only at the boundary of two adjacent words, word re-synchronization is possible after it is lost by burst error. The code is evaluated from the point of view of the overwrite noise, influence of the low frequency cut-off of the rotary transformer and side reading crosstalk noise at guardbandless recording of home use VCR. The result shows the code is suitable for this type of rotary head recording channel.

articleTitle: Effect of orientation ratio and powder properties on anhysteretic linearity of magnetic tape coatings
abstract: A generalized theory is developed to calculate the effects of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, bias current, coating thickness and anhysteretic linearity on Maximum Output Level in long-wavelength AC bias recording. The results are compared with data of .15" audio tapes. Is has been found, that the type of powder and orientation ratio are sources of variation of anhysteretic linearity.

articleTitle: Magnetization reversal in Y-Co permanent magnet particles observed by the vibrating reed magnetometer
abstract: The vibrating reed magnetometer (VRM) is a very sensitive tool for the investigation of magnetization processes in small particles of permanent magnet materials /1/, /2/. Using a modified version of this apparatus information about the magnetization reversal in uniaxially anisotropic Y-Co compounds is obtained from the magnetization jump fields in microscopic particles either under the influence of lower temperatures or as a function of the angle<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\vartheta_{o}</tex>between the easy axis of the magnetization and the external field. In Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>microparticles the variation of the shape of the magnetization loop with decreasing temperature reveals a striking proof for a nucleation-determined reversal process. This behaviour is supported by the variation of the experimentally observed jump fields for different orientation angles which can be fitted to a Kondorsky-type function.

articleTitle: Feasibility of passive damping from mixed-mu levitation
abstract: Mixed-mu levitation is the principle whereby iron is levitated with respect to s magnetising coil and stabilised by the proximity of diamagnetic super-conduction screen material. For application to MAGLEV ground transport, superconducting coils and stabilising screens are mounted on on-board cryogenic levitator pads, the vehicle levitating about a mild steel rail. To obtain adequate ride characteristics, auxilliary damping is required and passive damping schemes, if feasible, are preferred to active control schemes. The paper investigates the feasibility of passive damping utilising a secondary suspension and primary system employing copper Sheets attached to the cryostat. A full dynamic model of the suspension system is presented together with model predictions and feasibility criteria.

articleTitle: Dual-element, unshielded hall head
abstract: A new Hall-effect read head, consisting of either one or two thin InSb films perpendicular to the medium surface and incorporating no ferromagnetic materials, is proposed. The predicted performance of this head, obtained by numerical modeling, is better than that of inductive or magnetoresistive film heads, as well as that of ferrite heads. Because of the absence of ferromagnetic materials, this head generates no Barkhausen noise. Using the best presently available materials, its output voltage, signal-to-noise ratio and off-track performance are such that very high track densities - 100 tracks/mm (2500 tpi) and higher - are achievable.

articleTitle: Metal vapor vacuum arc switching: Applications and results
abstract: A generalized introduction to vacuum arc switching as relevant for EM launcher applications is presented. Advantages of vacuum switches are given for comparision with alternative switching devices. Issues of importance for megampere current operation are discussed. Results indicative of the capabilities of vacuum switches are presented.

articleTitle: Effect of Fe substitution on the magnetic characteristics of some RNi5alloys (R = Pr and Nd)
abstract: The magnetic properties of PrNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Fe and NdNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Fe have been studied at temperatures ranging from 4 to 300 K and at field strengths up to 21 kOe. Replacement of 20% of the Ni by Fe in PrNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>and NdNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>expands the lattice and produces a significant alteration in magnetic behavior. PrNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>is a Van Vleck paramagnet and NdNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>is a weak ferromagnet, Curie temperature = 13 K. In contrast, PrNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Fe and NdNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Fe are found to develop ferromagnetic order at low temperatures with Curie temperatures of 230 and 285 K, respectively. Saturation magnetizations at 4.2 K are found to be 7.0 and 7.3 μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>per formula unit for PrNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Fe and NdNi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>Fe, respectively. The magnetic behavior of these systems indicates that Fe induces a moment on the neighboring Ni atoms of about 0.65 μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>/Ni atom. The magnetization-temperature plots obtained for both systems below the Curie point, at 4 kOe applied field, show maxima. The maxima disappear in an applied field of 21 kOe, and hence they are attributed to the increased magnetic hardness at low temperatures.

articleTitle: Optical study of the coherence of Bloch walls motion during magnetization in Fe-Si 3% G.O. laminations
abstract: Through an optical technique making use of the Kerr effect, the motion of the Bloch walls on G.O. polycrystalline and single crystal Fe-Si strips is studied. The aim is to evidence the effects of internal fields on the wall motion, as produced by a driving field applied to the specimen. Results show that the motion of the walls in well oriented single crystal specimens is very little influenced by internal fields when displacements much larger then single Barkhausen jumps are taken into account. On the contrary, in polycrystalline G.O. specimens strong interaction effects arise, particularly in the low frequency components of the forced motion. Some implications of these results on the theory of the magnetic power loss are discussed.

articleTitle: Hyperfine-field-distribution of amorphous CoP saturated by high static fields
abstract: The hyperfine field distribution of an amorphous CoP sample with 22 at % P has been determined by NMR in large external fields between 1.2 T and 5.2 T. The maximum of the distribution appears at an hyperfine field of 17 T, the mean value is 13.8 T. From the enhancement factor it is found that the quadrupole coupling is very small and has no influence on the shape of the NMR spectrum.

articleTitle: Characterization of magnetites for monocomponent toner applications
abstract: The magnetic properties of 15 magnetite samples being considered for use in toners were determined. On the basis of magnetic and other physical properties, the samples were classified into three categories: (1) blocky precipitated particles; (2) acicular precipitated particles; and (3) comminuted natural magnetite. The distinguishing magnetic properties of each magnetite type are discussed. Equations accurately describing the magnetization curves of each sample and correlations among the various magnetic properties are described.

articleTitle: On the direct solution of two-dimensional eddy current problems
abstract: The validity of two-dimensional models of power frequency eddy current problems is extended by embedding the two-dimensional field region in three dimensions. External regions are represented by lumped parameter circuit elements, thus allowing generalized excitations, some nonlinearities, and the interconnection of several field regions in one system. An illustrative example is given, together with details of the numerical solution.

articleTitle: Historical review: 100 year's magnetic contributions to electrotechnics
Determination of the easy magnetic axis in SmIG
abstract: In this work, we shall present an experimental determination o£ the easy axis of samarium iron garnet at 4.2 K. At this temperature, the magnetization of a flux grown single crystal of SmiG has been measured in a steady magnetic field up to 150 kOe which lies either in a (110) plane containing the <111> directions or in a (100) plane containing the <210> directions. A linear field dependence of magnetization up to 150 kOe has been observed only when the field is applied along either a <110> or a <210> direction. A very pronounced anisotropic effect oil the reciprocal susceptibility has been evidenced in rotating magnetic field within the two planes. A maximum of the reciprocal magnetic susceptibility has been observed for the field parallel to <210> direction. A single ion theory accounts for the determination of the easy direction and for the evolution of this direction as a function of temperature.

articleTitle: Detector circuits for ternary coded magnetic recording
abstract: It has been shown [1] that the recording density ratio and the detection window can both be increased by the use of a ternary, i.e., 3-symbol, rather than binary recording technique. The three symbols, φ, 1 and 2 are represented in the media as absence of flux reversal, single reversal and two closely spaced reversals respectively. The implementation of coder and decoder for such a ternary code has been presented previously[2]. This paper presents a realization of detector circuits to distinguish Singlets (ones) and Doublets (twos) in the readback signal from each other and from noise and to detect the precise time-of-arrival for each of them. It also presents a slightly modified version of the code and points out how this simplifies the detector circuit.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of a fast electromagnetic actuator
abstract: The present paper is devoted to the modelling of a fast acting linear electromagnetic actuator in which the mechanical and electrical time constants are of the same order of magnitude. The computation of the electromagnetic and the mechanical quantities must then be performed simultaneously. This paper describes the algorithm used to solve both the Maxwell's equations and the equation of motion.

articleTitle: Hysteretic fields in a toroidal reactor
abstract: A modeling of hysteretic fields had been previously proposed for calculating three-dimensional magnetic fields in a toroidal reactor [1], This modeling of hysteretic fields is now generalized to include the anisotropic magnetization property caused by the lamination of iron sheets, and improved with respect to the time discretization method.

articleTitle: Design of low flying heads for floppy disk magnetic recording
abstract: Detailed calculations are presented for a realistic noncontact floppy disk/head interface. The numerical procedure is based on a factored-implicit finite difference algorithm which tracks a simultaneous solution of the air bearing and disk deflection asymptotically to steady-state. Examples are presented for a spherical head with either transverse or longitudinal ambient pressure slots. The slot is observed to draw off a portion of the air bearing flow rate and cause a reduction in flying height.

articleTitle: Lattice parameter and magnetization variation of CrSi-coated substituted gadolinium iron garnet films induced by heat treatment
abstract: The property variations of CrSi-coated epitaxial garnet films of composition (Gd,Bi)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Fe,Ga,Al)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>have been studied after heat treatments in air. Lattice constant increases and variations of the saturation magnetization which are described by the variations of the compensation temperature were observed. The lattice constant increase is determined by the introduction of oxygen vacancies as well as by the redistribution of Ga and Al between the octahedral and the tetrahedral lattice sites. The latter mechanism is of main importance for the change of the magnetization. The oxygen vacancy concentration can be increased by reducing the garnet film thickness and is probably terminated by the development of a diffusion barrier layer at the CrSi-garnet interface.

articleTitle: Magnetic cooling by an adiabatic spin reorientation
abstract: A new method of magnetic cooling is proposed by using an adiabatic entropy change associated with a spin reorientation transition. This is available for a magnetic refrigerator operating under a weaker magnetic field than an ordinary method using a superconducting magnet to cool a paramagnetic crystal. The single crystal and sintered samples of ErCrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>were adopted as a prototype material. The sample was set in the adiabatic cell and put in a sweeping magnetic field. The cooling was observed in the range from 2 to 11 K. A maximum cooling of 0.4 degrees was obtained for the single crystal just below the transition temperature TSR (= 9.8 K) in a magnetic field of 200 Oe after applying the correction of the demagnetizing effect. The entropy vs temperature diagram of ErCrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>was determined from measurements of the specific heat. The complete analogy between thermodynamic properties of the spin reorientation transition with those of a liquid-gas system suggests a possibility of an application to a heat engine. Such a device might be useful for maintaining a temperature lower than the transition temperature by a permanent magnet.

articleTitle: The influence of magnetic materials on the distribution of currents in conductors
abstract: The use of magnetic materials near the surface of current carrying conductors is of interest. A very noticeable change in the current distribution in flat conductors is found using rectangular magnetic bars. The current tends to concentrate at the air-gaps between the magnetic bars. Experimental results closely confirm the theory.

articleTitle: New form of unlaminated rotor motor
abstract: This paper reports on a new form of unlaminated rotor induction motor which has the characteristics of solid rotor motor at starting but with very much improved running performance. The motor has a hollow and unlaminated rotor. The outer surface of the rotor is left plain while the inner surface is fitted with cage winding. The motor employs two conventional polyphase stators. High starting torque to inertia ratio, high torque per unit volume and the ability to operate at three different speeds are some of the salient features of the motor. The motor performance is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: A method of approximating bubble domain runout diameter and bias magnetic field
abstract: Approximation formulae were derived to manually calculate bubble domain runout diameter d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>and bias magnetic field H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. A comparison of d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>calculated by these formulae with Thiele's results shows that the approximation formulae are accurate to within 3 percent.

articleTitle: Micromagnetic correlations in thin films
abstract: The influence of the structure defects on the micromagnetic properties of a thin film is investigated by means of the normalized autocorrelation ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>(r) of the magnetization. This concept leads to a natural understanding of the so-called "coupling volume" of HOFFMANN's ripple theory. Particularly we discuss HARTE's "random anisotropy model" on the basis of a realistic distribution of the size D of the crystallites in a polycrystalline material. Our numerical results reveal that the classical ripple theories have shortcomings, if the parameters of a film considerably differ from those of a typical permalloy film. Just that is the case in a number of modern materials considered for application.

articleTitle: Magnetoelastic effects and magnetic anisotropy in amorphous Fe-P alloys
abstract: The field dependences of elastic moduli were measured in electrodeposited amorphous Fe-P and Co-P tubes by resonance techniques at about 400 Hz and between 0.2 and 8 MHz. On account of magnetic anisotropies established during preparation (intrinsic anisotropy) and by field annealing, the magnetoelastic effects depended sensitively on the stress modes applied and the direction of the magnetizing field within the samples. The observations are consistent with a picture of the domain structure given in a previous paper Additionally it results that field annealing cannot destroy the intrinsic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Three dimensional finite element preprocessing of magnetic field problems
abstract: The ever increasing power of computers couples with the downward trend in memory costs have made it possible to solve very large complex field problems utilising the finite element methodology. This has emphasised the need for efficient data creation and handling which has stimulated investigation into what has become known as pre- and post- processing. Over the last decade a great deal of work has been done in pre- and post-processing as far as two dimensional analysis is concerned. However the level of expertise demonstrated with two dimensional problems is some way from being realised as far as three dimensional problems are concerned. This paper reports some of the details of element and constraint definition as implemented in a highly interactive three dimensional mesh generator designed to operate on a small dedicated computer.

articleTitle: Diffusion bonding of NiZn ferrite and nonmagnetic materials
abstract: Diffusion bonding of dissimilar ceramics can be accomplished by the application of pressure only while the ceramics are at a temperature where their respective thermal expansion curves cross. A process for manufacturing magnetic head cores is disclosed wnere a NiZn ferrite is bonded by diffusion co a nonmagnetic ceramic by heating the core pieces to the crossover temperature and them applying the bonding pressure. The pressure can be removed either before or after the bonded pieces are cooled.

articleTitle: A general mixed boundary conditions definition for eddy current problems
abstract: The authors present a new method to compute the current distribution (eddy currents or conduction currents) in a solid or liquid material with boundaries made of another thin and conducting material. In this configuration numerical methods such as finite element techniques are unavailable due to the thickness of the boundary to be meshed. The authors propose to use a special finite element called "boundary element" and to introduce the characteristics of the containing medium into the boundary conditions applied to the main conducting material. The techniques for solving problems with such mixed boundary conditions are exposed and results for some conduction problems are given.

articleTitle: Influence of the sign and magnitude of the magnetostriction constant λson magnetoelastic properties
abstract: The influence of the sign and the magnitude magnetostriction constant λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>on various physical properties was studied. The stress dependence of the hysteresis, of the electrical resistivity, the Mössbauer hyperfine field and the neutron depolarisation was measured on ribbons with λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>> 0 and λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>< 0. The change of the Young's modulus with the external stress and the applied field also sensitively reflects the sign of λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>as demonstrated on Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</inf>.

articleTitle: Comparison of reproduction performance of a single pole head and a ring head
abstract: The reproduction pulse amplitude of a single pole head from double-layer perpendicular media has been analyzed. We derived an analytic expression to relate the pulse amplitude to the head and medium parameters. Experimental data are also presented to verify the calculated results. The reproduction performances of a single pole head and a ring head are theoretically compared and found to be comparable when both are normalized to the same head inductance.

articleTitle: Soft magnetic toners: A simple analytic model
abstract: Soft magnetic toners, made of magnetic pigments dispersed in a polymer matrix, are modeled. The pigments, roughly spherical in shape, are assumed multidomain and isotropic. The input parameters are the initial intrinsic susceptibility of the pigments, their volume fraction and the particle packing factor of the bulk powder. The analyzis proceeds through 3 steps : (a) microscopic analysis at pigment level, (b) macroscopic analysis at toner particle level, (c) gigascopic analysis at bulk powder level, which usually is the only source of measured data. Demagnetizing fields are taken into account as well as interaction fields which are synthetically modeled to match known limiting cases. A set of analytic formula is derived that, for each of the above levels, relates the apparent initial susceptibility to the input parameters. Applications and experimental verifications are described.

articleTitle: Worst case code patterns for magnetic buried servos
abstract: A technique for determining worst case run-length-limited (RLL) code patterns for data-to-servo coupling in magnetic buried servos is presented. The problem is reduced to a general dynamic programming problem, whose solution is described. The general problem can require large amounts of computation, so a method is also developed to determine approximate worst case patterns by solving a classical dynamic programming problem using the Viterbi algorithm. An error estimate for the approximate solution is also derived. Computational results are presented for the

articleTitle: Multi input-output control of magnetically suspended linear guide
abstract: A magnetic suspension system for manufacturing or other use is presented. A contactless linear guide for the use of a manufacturing instrument and peripheral equipment requires a simple structure and high stability against disturbances since frequent starts and stops are carried out by fairly large driving forces. The construction proposed here has two reference guide bars and a carrier with six control magnets. A linearized multi magnet suspension system and the regulator control are described and also the computational and experimental results are shown.

articleTitle: Domain modifications due to compression perpendicular to the rolling direction of coated HI-B sheets
abstract: Domain modifications due to compressive stress applied perpendicular to the rolling direction (RD) of coated HI-B sheets are discussed. Both single and stacked sheets were investigated. Compressive stress normal to the sheet surface, as well as compressive stress within the sheet plane, was found to cause refinement of the main domain structure. The degree of refinement increased considerably with increasing initial domain width in the unstressed demagnetized sample. The major refinement occurred for applied pressures up to about 1.5 MPa and 3 MPa in the stacked and unstacked case, respectively. The practical importance of these effects is discussed. Possibilities of using them in a beneficial way by increasing the tension in the core bandages are considered.

articleTitle: A proposal on a generalized method for constructing the fixed-length adaptive block recording code
abstract: A simple and more generalized algorithm is presented for the design of a fixed-length adaptive block recording code, named the (d, k; m, n) code where d and k are the minimum and maximum run-length of the same symbol, and m and n are the dataword and codeword lengths. This algorithm is based on systematic use of both lookback and lookahead informations and an expanded version of the merging rule by Jacoby. Applications of this algorithm to (2, 9; 3, 6) and (2, 8; 4, 8) NRZI waveform codes are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A high performance embedded servo system
abstract: The design and analysis of a high performance embedded or sector servo system is presented. The advances in the embedded servo system yield increased positioning accuracy, reduced settling time, and reduced sensitivity to missed or rejected sector(s). A servo system suitable for an one hundred ninety six tracks per centimeter cartridge disk drive with under two millisecond fixed/removable settling time has been demonstrated. The two and one-half (2 1/2) percent of the data storage area occupied by the thirty two (32) embedded servo sectors demonstrated a track density comparable to non-removeable disk files using three and two-tenths (3 2/10) percent.

articleTitle: Transient response of coaxial pulse coils
abstract: Of central importance in designing coaxial launcher systems is understanding the mechanical response and structual limits of the magnetic pulse coils. In normal operation the driving frequency can vary from static conditions through the lowest natural modes to well beyond the highest frequencies. By using a lumped parameter model the transient behavior of a magnetic pulse coil can be readily characterized. In an effort to understand the failure mechanism of coaxial pulse coils the results of this model are compared to the experimental performance of several thin build coils.

articleTitle: New high gain pulse-triggered power transistors with amorphous saturable CT cores
abstract: A new high gain pulse-triggered power transistor (PTPT) with amorphous saturable CT (current transformer) is presented. In the PTPT, a current transformer plays an important role in the astable multivibrator operation. The base of power transistors can be directly driven by the collector current through the current transformer. This positive feedback operation holds the on state of the power transistor by initiating the small trigger pulse to the primary winding of the current transformer. Turn off operation can be also achieved applying trigger pulse. This behavior corresponds to the so called GTO (GATE TURN-OFF THYRISTOR). A turn off technique is developed to extinguish the conducting power transistor. In this paper, the switching characteristics of PTPT and its experimental results are described. New applications using PTPT are also introduced.

articleTitle: Influence of ionic migration induced by heat treatment on the Faraday rotation of PrxY3-xGayFe5-yO12garnets
abstract: The Faraday rotation of a Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.08</inf>Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.92</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.11</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.89</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>single crystal has been measured at 1.15 μm wavelength for 77< T <300 K and magnetic field applied along the [111] direction after different heat treatments. These heat treatments consisted of annealing under oxygene atmosphere at 1073, 1123, 1300 and 1473 K during a time long enough to allow the migration of gallium between the "a" and "d" ferric sites followed by quenching in air. The spontaneous rotation of this garnet which is negative (with respect to the positive Faraday rotation of YIG) increases in absolute value when the annealing temperature is increased. The Pr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>rotation ΔΘ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>, is extracted from the data assuming that the Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>ions behaviour is similar in Pr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>:YIG and Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>:YIG. Using the Van Erk thermodynamic model with the same gallium stabilization energies in "a" and "d" sites as in Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>:YIG, we observe a linear relationship between ΔΘ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>and the Ga<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>content in tetrahedral sites.

articleTitle: Mossbauer studies in sputtered A-Fe80B20foils
abstract: Mossbauer studies have been carried out on sputtered amorphous Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">80</inf>B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf>foils in the temperature range of 4.4 K to 300 K. The results have been analysed using Window's method. The coefficients B and C in Bloch's law are evaluated from the data. One finds a smaller value of B in sputtered foils in comparison to the liquid quenched ribbons. There are indications that the mean square range of exchange interaction is larger in these foils.

articleTitle: Some aspects of the computer aided design of recording heads
abstract: A general purpose finite element post-processing system implemented on a PDP-11 or a VAX computer is described. The system is applied to the analysis of recording head design and shows examples of a perpendicular head. The package provides the designer with a set of vector and scalar operations with which to manipulate a field solution and a powerful display facility for examining the results.

articleTitle: Development of a modular electromagnetic launcher system for the air force armament laboratory
abstract: An electromagnetic launcher (EML) system was developed for the Air Force Armament Laboratory (AFATL) to use in studying all aspects of rail accelerators. The EML accelerates 10 g arc-driven projectiles to velocities >3 km/s. It employs 4 m rails, has a 10 mm circular bore, and is driven by a low-impedance pulse-forming network (PFN) capable of delivering 250 kJ with a peak current of 450 kA and pulse length of 1.8 ms. Key design features include (1) preacceleration to minimize arc erosion of rails, (2) a projectile fuse that ignites the arc and eliminates external switching, and (3) careful matching of EML and PFN impedances at the current peak to maximize energy transfer to the arc. The EML's helium-driven preaccelerator propels the projectile to 500 m/s before it enters the rail accelerator. Power comes from five PFN modules charged to 800 V. Values of network elements are easily adjusted to change pulse characteristics for exploring a wide range of EML parameters. AFATL has written an EML modeling code that simulates all power source configurations. The EML system and code will be used to improve efficiency and reliability and to optimize components of a potential EML weapon.

articleTitle: Domain structure of a 5% Si-Fe single crystal with Néel orientation
abstract: The influence of different thermomagnetic preparatory treatments of a 5% Si-Fe single crystal with Néel orientation on the behaviour of the magnetic domain structure was investigated by means of the Kerr magneto-optic effect. The crystal was cooled down from 600°C to room temperature applying different kinds of magnetic fields, which leads to various kinds of behaviour of the domain widths depending on the actual magnetic field strength and temperature, caused by the induced magnetic anisotropy. Since the magnetic anisotropy constant depends on the silicon content, the results of the measurements with the crystal containing 5% Si are compared with results of those with crystals containing 2.5% Si reported in earlier papers.

articleTitle: Switching for electric rail guns
abstract: A single stage rail gun driven from an inductive energy store requires a direct commutation switch. The high current levels and long conduction times dictate a fresh approach to the switch. This paper examines the commutation event and describes a successful 500 kA direct commutation rail gun switch.

articleTitle: New fabrication technique for magnetic bubble circuits with submicron dimensions
abstract: A new technique which permits the fabrication of submicrometer bubble propagation circuits has been described. Straight line patterns and contiguous zigzag patterns are combined with an appropriate registration to form bubble propagation patterns. The straight line pattern width corresponds to the gap width in the Permalloy bubble propagation circuits. By controlling the exposure time in fabricating straight line photoresist patterns, submicrometer pattern gaps are easily obtained using photomasks with 1 μm minimum features. The 4 μm period and 0.5 μm gap width permalloy circuits fabricated using this technique provide promising propagation characteristics for 1 μm bubbles: 60 Oe bias field margin at 60 Oe drive field and 25 Oe minimum propagation drive field.

articleTitle: Induced magnetic anisotropy generated by annealing in implanted garnets
abstract: A field-induced anisotropy may be generated into hydrogen implanted garnet layers by annealing at temperatures below the Curie point and it can be destroyed by annealing above T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>'. The presence of neon in the implanted layer lowers the induced effect.

articleTitle: Triplex code for quarternary high density recording
abstract: Triplex is a newly conceived high information density code compatible with present day digital recording systems. It conveys data on position (phase), polarity (transition direction) and amplitude (breakwidth) and offers efficient overwrite, self-clocking and a generous window margin. For a two amplitude level encoding scheme, n cells can be mapped into 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>-1 symbols in triplex as opposed to 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>in MFM code. This corresponds to 130% increase in information density over MFM. Triplex offers one of the highest density ratios practically realizable in the domain of saturated digital magnetic recording.

articleTitle: Magnetism in science, business, and everyday life
A coaxial radial opening switch for a distributed- energy-store rail launcher
abstract: The current electromagnetic launch technology base suggests that a distributed-energy-store railgun may be an attractive alternative to chemical rockets for Earth-to-space launch. If homopolar generator-charged inductors are to serve as the basic energy stores, a difficult switching problem must be overcome. Several switching schemes (arc, liquid metal, and electromagnetic) have been investigated. Studies indicate that arc opening switches would prove to be to destructive when used with continuous rail launcher systems. The most attractive alternative is an electromagnetically actuated switching scheme. The operation, calculated performance, fabrication, and initial testing of a switch based upon this scheme is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Steady-state behaviour of a magnetic frequency quintupler
abstract: In the paper a magnetic frequency quintupler of transformer type is considered. Starting from the symmetry conditions, a single-core equivalent circuit is proposed and serves as an aid in carrying a steady-state analysis. The mathematical model applied permits determination of core flux density and also all quintupler quantities under various load conditions as well as prediction of ferroresonant phenomena. Galerkin's procedure is employed under the assumption of four flux density harmonics in the core in order to obtain nonlinear algebraic equations which are solved by direct application of the Newton-Raphson method. Results of analysis are presented and on being related to the physical characteristics of the quintupler prove to have very good accuracy.

articleTitle: Diffusion bonded matrix of HGMF for BWR condensate water purification
abstract: In the application of HGMF for a nuclear power plant, especially for the BWR, matrix reliability as well as crud removal efficiency is important. A new matrix called Diffusion Bonded Matrix has been developed. Test results are reported using a HGMF test unit consisting of a 160 mm diameter × 240 mm long matrix. The filtering velocity and the magnetic flux density used in these tests were 800m/h and 5kG respectively. The filtering efficiency for an artificial crud (α-Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), of 85% to 100% was obtained for the new matrix. The new matrix indicated slightly excellent crud removal efficiency than that by the conventional wool matrix under the same filtering conditions. And the new matrix kept its original mechanical strength and had very few fiber breakage, while the conventional wool matrix lost its volume elasticity and the washed-out pieces of fibers were observed. These results demonstrate the great applicability of the new matrix for the condensate water treatment of the BWR.

articleTitle: Computing procedure of mutual reactances in multiwinding transformers
abstract: A general computing procedure is described for determining the equivalent network of a transformer with two or more concentric windings divided into multiaxial coils. The magnetic field of a transformer is considered and the equations are discretized by means of the finite element method. Taking into account the winding connections the machine equations are written such that the machine mutual reactances can be calculated simultaneously. A three-phase multiwinding transformer is considered, the mutual reactance values of which have been measured. The average discrepancies between the calculated and measured values are less than 10-15 percent.

articleTitle: The effect of thermal activation and quantum-mechanical tunneling on the AC-susceptibility
abstract: The ac-susceptibility χ of a ferromagnetic Ni-base alloy has been measured below 5K. The experimental data can be represented by a relation derived earlier for the unidirectional motion of 180°-domain walls. This relation is based on the assumption that the mobility of 180°-domain walls is governed by their interaction with obstacles present in the specimen. These pinning centers are overcome by combinations of thermal activation and quantum-mechanical tunneling.

articleTitle: Highly accurate measurements within the international system of units
abstract: Physics today presents a consistent model of natural phenomena based upon a coherent system of units of physical quantities. Knowledge of the most accurate values of the most important fundamental constants is essential for the traceability of units and for the refinement of theory. Of the four base units in the International System of units relevant to electrodynamics, the ampere can as yet only be realized with poor relative uncertainty of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>; the same holds true for the derived electric and magnetic units with the exception of the ohm. The accurate measurement of the gyromagnetic ratio of the proton γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>promises to yield a more accurate realization of the ampere than that achieved using the traditional current balance.

articleTitle: Design and testing of a magnetically operated rep-rate opening switch
abstract: A magnetically operated opening switch was designed to divert current from an inductive store into an electromagnetic launcher. The switch was designed to be operated repetitively on command (i.e., noncyclically). A laboratory development switch was designed, fabricated, and extensively tested to determine electrical and mechanical operating properties. The switch has been repetitively tested with contact currents as high as 30 kA, corresponding to contact current densities of 500 MA/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Opening times of less than 300 microseconds are regularly observed. The switch can also be used to shunt current from the launcher when desired projectile velocities have been achieved, thereby conserving inductor energy. Closing times of 200 microseconds were observed in this mode. The effects of lead impedance on opening characterisitics are reported.

articleTitle: Static and dynamic studies of bubble wall states in tilted ion implanted garnets
abstract: Two kinds of bubbles, small circular bubbles and normal elliptical bubbles, have been observed at the same bias field in [111] misoriented (YSm Lu Ca)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Fe Ge)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>H+ implanted samples. Static and dynamic experiments were performed on these bubbles in order to characterize them. Strong in-plane orthorombic like anisotropy exists in these samples and these two kinds of bubbles may be correlated with the eight wall states observed by Konishi in [110] oriented garnet films. Transitions from normal to small bubbles occured only when the in-plane field was applied along the easy axis of magnetization of the implanted layer. The behaviour of closure domains seems to be preponderant for driving the observed transitions.

articleTitle: Homogeneity and thermal behaviour of non-crystalline rare earth iron oxides studied by Mossbauer spectroscopy
abstract: We report measurements to test the homogeneity and the thermal annealing behaviour of non crystalline (nc) rare earth iron oxides prepared by dc-sputtering. The Mossbauer spectra show that the slowly deposited samples are homogeneous with respect to their thickness. The thermal annealing experiments reveal, that the oxygen deficiency, which is introduced by the sputter process, can be removed prior to crystallization. This proves, that this deficiency is not necessary to stabilize the nc structure.

articleTitle: Lamination permeability calculated from a field-strength-dependent material permeability
abstract: A method is described whereby the permeability of soft magnetic laminations can be calculated from a material permeability of different dependences on field strength. Computer-aided solutions are given for typical laminations, magnetic qualities, and rise functions of material permeability. The results are compared with those calculated using an earlier theory based on a field-strength-independent material permeability. Limits in permeability rise are derived up to which the latter method can be used with tolerable differences. The extended method may further be used at higher flux densities, including cases of magnetic anisotropy.

articleTitle: Influence of annealing on magnetization, Faraday rotation, and optical absorption of high-energy heavy ion irradiated garnet films
abstract: Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>(YIG) and Gd<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>(GIG) films have been irradiated with 238U ions of specific energy 1.4 MeV per nucleon. The temperature dependences of the saturation polarization, I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, and of the Faraday rotation Θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>(λ = 633 nm), and at T = 293 K the spectra of the Faraday rotation and of the optical absorption of the YIG films were measured after various annealing treatments. Annealing of films damaged by ion irradiation leads to an increase of the Faraday rotation of YIG and GIG. In YIG a 4.3 times higher value than in the as-grown film can be created at low temperatures. This strong Θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>enhancement is attributed to a line broadening of the optical transitions.

articleTitle: Planar YIG filters
abstract: A tunable filter is described which uses spherical crystals of magnetic materials such as Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) together with photolithographically fabricated coupling structures. Eddy current induced frequency shifts can be completely avoided in this structure and eddy-current induced line-broadening can be reduced to an insignificant level. Precise crystal orientation, required to avoid temperature dependence of the resonant frequency, is achieved by an improved sphere orienting technique.

articleTitle: Reclamping error analysis for a removable disk drive
abstract: A removable disk drive is a rotating machine where the disk may be clamped and released many times on the drive spindle. The errors produced in the process when the clamping axis does not coincide with the axis of rotation are studied here. Simple expressions are obtained for the statistical expectation M (A) and variance σ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(A) where A is a random variable such as "off-track". Error contribution caused by component tolerances of the disk, the clamp, the spindle and the bearings. One general and two particular cases are considered.

articleTitle: Measurement of magnetic parameters of bubble films by ferrimagnetic resonance and ferrimagnetic antiresonance
abstract: Ferrimagnetic resonance and ferrimagnetic antiresonance are used to measure the magnetic parameters (magnetization, perpendicular uniaxial anisotropy, magnetocrystalline anisotropy and g-factor) characterizing the bubble material MnCr-ferrite.

articleTitle: Magnetic field of a ring head on a double layer medium
abstract: A simple theoretical model is developed for a Karlquist-type recording head interacting with a two layer recording medium in which the sublayer has a high but finite permeability. During readback the vertical H fields far from the gap are shown to decay exponentially with a characteristic length r given by<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r = t \ast h \ast u</tex>where t is the sublayer thickness, h is the spacing between the head and the sublayer, and u is the relative permeability of the sublayer. The long tails of this field account for observed readback wave forms. The model also predicts that the spatial extent of sublayer saturation during the write process will be twenty to one hundred gap lengths, justifying the assumption that during write one may ignore the sublayer. The write prediction was tested experimentally by making a standstill recording with a Winchester-type head on a double layer medium and measuring the fringing field above the medium with a high-resolution Hall probe. The data were compared to the predictions of an iterative simulation in which the sublayer was either present or absent during write. A significantly better fit was found when the simulated medium contained no sublayer during the write process.

articleTitle: Design and use of a superconducting solenoid type magnetic separator in mineral processing
abstract: In mineral processing, the conventional magnetic separators are equiped with traditionnal magnetic circuits which develop a magnetic field of less than 2 T. The use of these circuits has nevertheless many disadvantages which are : magnetic saturation is easily reached, remanent field causes clogging, equipments are heavy, bulky and high energy consumption. Only a separator having a superconducting solenoid can contribute in solving most of the problems and produce high magnetic field (7 T). This paper presents and describes a magnetic separator with a superconducting solenoid with integrated closed circuit for helium liquefaction. The system generator and maintenance is simplified by extensive automation realized by a versatile programmable autocontrol unit. Comparative study : 1) Concentration of fine itabirite iron ore gives a concentrate of 68 % Fe and a recovery rate of > 98 % 2) Purification of raw materials such as glass sand and syenite nephelinie produces a purified concentrate with a lower content of paramagnetic minerals and reduces the operating costs (energy consumption).

articleTitle: Further development of plasma-armature railgun simulation codes at MRL
abstract: We present a critique of present railgun armature simulation codes and discuss the further development of such codes for railguns in the light of recent experimental findings. It is concluded that present models of the plasma are inadequate and that we require a model which is insensitive to the ion species making up the plasma, and which maintains constant plasma volume except for very low currents in the system. Further work includes the need to consider current distributions in the armature region, as well as the need to include the effects of friction of the projectile in the barrel.

articleTitle: Poynting vector distribution within the magnetic boundary layers of magneto-fluid interactions
abstract: Behavioral indentifications have been established for the electric field intensity, induced magnetic current and poynting vector distribution within the magnetic boundary layer of the magneto-fluid interactions in a two parallel plate MHD channel. Major impulsive changes in distributions are detected in close proximity of the applied magnetic field source, both in the up-stream and down-stream regions.

articleTitle: Error theory for laser etched disk standards
abstract: An electromagnetic model and a geometric model are proposed for readback errors caused by laser etching of a magnetic disk surface. These models enable calculation of expected extra pulse (drop-in) and missing pulse (drop-out) error counts for the design and analysis of error standards for magnetic disk testing. In most cases a geometric approach is adequate for the analysis of missing pulses but not for extra pulses. A practical formula is derived for the calculation of extra pulse amplitude ratios from laser etching, and the effect of demagnetization at the laser etch is estimated.

articleTitle: The use of permanent magnets and adjustment principles in miniaturizing modern relays
abstract: Besides their main function of providing flux, permanent magnets - especially ferrites - can be utilized in a number of different ways. In the course of relay miniaturization the permanent magnet's functions increase therefore in complexity and number, which results in considerably better matching of magnetic circuits and improved sensitivity to operating current. The multifunctional properties of the permanent magnets are discussed and explained using several designs of miniaturized relays - preferably bistable relays - as examples. Mechanical variations due to production processes can be compensated for by optimized more efficient adjustment methods. Therefore the required functional values can be obtained more reliably and economically. Due to miniaturization relays will continue to be used in a large number of electronic circuit applications.

articleTitle: There is no limit to creativity - The development of magnetic recording technology in Japan
Producibility improvements and manufacture of a prototype commercial compact pulsed homopolar generator
Synthesis of sodium-zinc spinel ferrites
abstract: The synthesis of spinel ferrites with composition Zn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-2x</inf>Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>has been performed and the composition range in which single phase samples are obtained has been defined. The characterization of the samples has been carried out from atomic absorption and X-ray fluorescence analyses, X-ray diffraction patterns, Mössbauer spectroscopy and thermomagnetic measurements. It is show that significant loss of Na does exist when the synthesis is performed at high temperatures. When the Na volatilization is avoided spinel oxides with Na content up to 0.25 atoms per unit formula can be obtained. In this case the increase of the interatomic distances leads to differing fundamental magnetic properties as compared to the equivalent lithium-zinc ferrites.

articleTitle: Improvement of magnetic properties of 34Ni-29Co-3Mo-Fe alloy by adjusting the composition and controlling the textures of recrystallization
abstract: In order to improve the magnetic properties of 34Ni -29Co-3Mo-Fe alloy, two types of new alloys have been developed by adjusting the composition and controlling the textures of recrystallization:35Ni-27Co-3Mo-Fe(Ku<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\gg</tex>Kl) and 34Ni-29Co-4Mo-Fe(Ku≐Kl). These alloys not only retain the high saturation induction of original al -loy(Bs=15800G), but also possess some other better mag -netic properties respectively, i.e, for the first alloy μm=117.5 * 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>G/Oe and Br/Bs=0.992, and the second alloy: μ5=5.24 * 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, μ10=14.2 * 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, and P1.0/400=0.89w/kg. The two alloys can meet different requirements for various types of electronic devices. The first new alloy may be used to make cores of bidirectional pulse transformers, magnetic modulators and transformers with adjustable pulse width etc. The second new alloy may make D.C.conversions etc.

articleTitle: Eddy current induction in flat screens of a microwave cavity
abstract: The eddy currents induced in flat screens of an EPR spectrometer microwave cavity by a time-harmonic modulating magnetic field are analysed. The screens are assumed to be thin as compared to the skin depth and the eddy currents are considered as surface currents. The problem is formulated as an integro-differential equation using a scalar potential representation of eddy currents. The numerical solution is performed by means of the finite element method. The results show the influence of additional cuts in the screen on electromagnetic field quantities.

articleTitle: New ion-implantation method for 4-µm period bubble device
abstract: It is well-known that bubble propagation margins for ion-implanted bubble devices depend strongly on ion-implantation conditions. A new ion-implantation method is reported that can significantly improve bubble propagation margins for minor loops with 4 × 4 μm bit cell size. The implantation was done through a Mo thin film layer so that the lattice strain and the anisotropy field change would be more uniform through the depth of the implanted layer. With this method, minor loops can be formed by hydrogen single implantation. Consequently simplification of the implantation process is achieved.

articleTitle: 2D correcting of magnetic field inhomogeneities
